result.coreDiagnosis: The candidate's extreme job hopping (4 roles in ~3.5 years, 3 under 6 months) signals a critical lack of sustained ownership and deep technical partnership required for a mid-level Product Manager (Technical) role.
result.roleFitVerdict: Profile reads as a high-velocity, generalist Associate PM with some technical exposure, but the short tenures and smaller-scale impacts don't align with the sustained technical ownership and engineer trust expected for this mid-level PM-T role.
recruiterScan: (Risk) Significant job hopping: 4 roles in ~3 years 3 months, with 3 roles lasting less than 6 months, indicating a critical lack of sustained ownership.
(Level) Impact scale leans small-to-mid market: WAUs of 1,000-1,400 and B2B SaaS ARR of $1.5M, not demonstrating FAANG-tier scale or complexity for a mid-level PM-T.
(Stack) LLM/AI experience is present (prompt engineering, LLM APIs), but the depth of technical tradeoff judgment and system architecture involvement isn't clearly articulated for a PM-T role.
(Metrics) Good quantification of impact for many bullets, but some are 'estimated' (15-20% reply rates) or lack baseline numbers, which reduces credibility for a technical role focused on outcomes.

topHiringRisks.title: Lack of Sustained Technical Ownership
topHiringRisks.description: The candidate's extreme job hopping (4 roles in ~3.5 years, with 3 roles under 6 months) makes it impossible to demonstrate sustained end-to-end ownership of a product area, build deep technical understanding, or earn engineer trust over time, all crucial for a mid-level PM-T.

topHiringRisks.title: Insufficient Technical Depth for PM-T
topHiringRisks.description: While the resume lists AI/LLM tools and 're-architected' some systems, the descriptions lack specific examples of technical tradeoff discussions, deep architectural understanding, or direct collaboration with engineering on complex system design decisions, which are core to a 'Technical' PM role.

topHiringRisks.title: Scale Mismatch for Mid-Level PM-T
topHiringRisks.description: Quantified impacts, while positive, often reference smaller user bases (e.g., 1,000-1,400 WAUs) or internal system improvements without clearly articulating the technical complexity or scale of the underlying systems, which is a mismatch for the expected scope of a mid-level PM-T at a high-growth company.

rewriteExample.before: Lifting first-week campaign-launch rate among new accounts, and enabling reps to scale campaign volume without added headcount.
rewriteExample.after: Lifted first-week campaign-launch rate 25% (from 40% to 65%) for new accounts by re-architecting the multi-step LinkedIn campaign builder with conditional branching logic, enabling 2x rep productivity and 15% increase in weekly campaign volume.
rewriteExample.explanation: The original phrase was qualitative. The rewrite adds specific, measurable outcomes (25% lift, 40% to 65% baseline) and quantifies the business impact (2x rep productivity, 15% campaign volume increase), directly addressing the 'outcome metrics' and 'system outcomes' expectations for a technical PM role.
